We formulate this as a probabilistic graphical model where each player pair forms a 'bond' with an associated energy cost. Transitions between match-ups occur via bond-breaking and formation, governed by a Gibbs distribution that penalizes high-energy configurations. This approach naturally handles uncertainty and allows for systematic comparison across different defensive strategies. The resulting algorithms map directly onto particle filtering and reinforcement learning frameworks, providing a unified computational bridge between statistical physics and modern machine learning.
